messages.author: 936ef8c6d12fc338
messages.subject: pc.prec doesn't constrain variance
parts:
Dear all,

I'm using a negative binomial model with f(LocationID, model = "iid", constr = TRUE, hyper = list(theta = list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(1, 1e-9)))). The estimated median precision of this random effect is 0.39, which is much too small given the prior. Changing the alpha parameter of the prior has no impact on the posterior. What is going on here?

There are about 800 locations, each with about 100 observations. The top 10 random effects have a mean ranging from 3.6 to 4.7. The associated observations range from 6 to 516 (5%/95% quantile). The top 10 lowest random effects have a mean ranging from -3.7 to -3.3. The associated observations range from 0 to 1. Only 4 non-zero observations per locations.

Best regards,

Thierry

parts:
So this means and lambda is about 20, like the prior for the stdev is
exponential with rate 20. see below:

seems like the data dominates the prior in this case.

> inla.pc.dprec
function (prec, u, alpha, lambda, log = FALSE)
{
lambda = inla.pc.prec.lambda(u, alpha, lambda)
s = 1/sqrt(prec)
d = dexp(s, rate = lambda, log = log)
log.jac = -log(2) - 3/2 * log(prec)
if (log) {
return(d + log.jac)
}
else {
return(d * exp(log.jac))
}
}

The “canonical” pc precision I would say is three times the SD of the output. Perhaps this is just the data dominating the prior as H indicates, but I wonder if a prior more along those lines, perhaps mindful of / adjusted for the error family, would be more usefully informative.

Jonathan
